items.title: George "Kid Sheik" Colar Interview, 1958-07-20
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...if you hear records of Jimmy Noon... is there somebody who would remind you somehow, the style of George the Boyd? [INTERVIEWEE] No, see, George the Boyd, he's still got the New Orleans style...

ctx.x: Well, I'd say right now, see, George the Boyd was a clarinet player playing a thing, you know. Nice toarnation, you know. And right now, I mean, just like I'd figure, well, George Lewis is, I mean, is playing, uh, Planet Client at Moe Client at, and what George the Boyd's playing during the time, because George was playing better, but the time, advanced it, and the company got faster, and George is playing Planet Client. Oh, yes, yes, yes. And I will say, at the time when George the Boyd was playing, he was…

No, but I mean, somebody whose style reminds you of George the Boyd. For example, if you hear records of Jimmy Noon, or of Johnny Dodds, or some, somebody else, is there somebody who would remind you somehow, the style of George the Boyd?

No, see, George the Boyd, he's still got the New Orleans style, and George Lewis, they just say, that variation, they just, you know, they say, I mean, I could almost tell, uh, uh, uh, uh, take a Planet player, if he's not from New Orleans, I can mostly tell his style of playing, because I know the average, uh, the Planet player style would've been playing. I know George the Boyd style, Boyd Banks style, Reddick on me, all them fellas style. And, uh, George the Boyd and George Lewis mostly varies, fast varies,…
